open_errors.issue: Under the agreed day count (F290: the Fair is at dawn of day 20, and remaining days = 20 minus the day number, so eleven remain on day 9), the ribs lie at first light falls on day 4. Sixteen days remain then, not seventeen, and fifteen remain once that day is lost.
open_errors.fix: Change the dawn count to sixteen and the night count to fifteen.

patches.find: She would take a day, perhaps two, and he had seventeen left and a regent counting them for him.
patches.replace: She would take a day, perhaps two, and he had sixteen left and a regent counting them for him.

patches.find: The day was gone. Sixteen of the twenty, then, and he had spent one on his own pride.
patches.replace: The day was gone. Fifteen of the twenty, then, and he had spent one on his own pride.

open_errors.issue: In ch 2 Rohan sends the other wardens back to the post, so only Varun crosses with him. In ch 3, on the gully, Rohan 'went to find his men', but he has no men there.
open_errors.fix: He goes to find his lieutenant.

patches.find: said Rohan, and went to find his men.
patches.replace: said Rohan, and went to find his lieutenant.

open_errors.issue: Asha's deadline, set on day 7 in ch 10, ran to dusk of the next day (day 8, ch 12). Lalit guides the hunters on the night of day 9, a full day past the deadline. Meera says Asha 'hasn't waited an hour past it'.

patches.find: She gave me the day and the next until the light went, and she hasn't waited an hour past it.
patches.replace: She gave me the day and the next until the light went, and she hasn't waited a day past it.

open_errors.issue: The Closing Law was written 60 winters before Book 1 and Rohan is 35. The law was therefore written about 25 winters before he was born, not 'sixty winters before he was born'.
open_errors.fix: Say the law was written sixty winters ago, long before he was born.

patches.find: He could have said the warden-judge, or the queen, or the Closing Law itself, written sixty winters before he was born.
patches.replace: He could have said the warden-judge, or the queen, or the Closing Law itself, written sixty winters ago, long before he was born.

open_errors.issue: Ch 17 says Varun held Rohan's horse 'when Rohan was newly captain' and calls them ten years friends. Ch 2 and ch 16 also say ten years. Ch 31 says Rohan held the post's seal as captain for twelve winters.
open_errors.fix: Make the seal tenure ten winters to match the ten-year captaincy.

patches.find: Rohan had held the only seal on that road for twelve winters.
patches.replace: Rohan had held the only seal on that road for ten winters.

open_errors.issue: Rohan says he vowed to keep the law 'in the Teeth'. He made no such statement on the Goat's Teeth in ch 15. He defended the law in the Rope-Hut (ch 13 and 14).
open_errors.fix: Place the earlier statement in the Rope-Hut.

patches.find: I said I would, in the Teeth. I said it at the grave.
patches.replace: I said I would, in the Rope-Hut. I said it at the grave.

open_errors.issue: In ch 19 Rohan makes a bound promise: 'Until then I carry every bucket.' In ch 21, before the doors shut, the text reads as if Nimmi is the one carrying two buckets ('She set both buckets down'). Read literally, that breaks a bound promise with no great-lie cost. Later in the same scene Rohan picks the buckets up.
open_errors.fix: Make the buckets Rohan's from the start of the scene.

patches.find: Nimmi caught him in the lane with a bucket in each hand and no patience.
patches.replace: Nimmi caught him in the lane, a bucket in each of his hands, and she had no patience.

patches.find: She set both buckets down on the frozen mud.
patches.replace: He set both buckets down on the frozen mud.

open_errors.issue: The book states that a lone crosser loses the path within the hour and the mountain takes them (ch 3). In ch 22, Dilan follows Kiran's tracks alone up to the waystone with no sign of the same failure. This makes a solo crossing look survivable.
open_errors.fix: Show that Dilan had lost the line too and was failing when they met.

patches.find: There was a warden there. He'd been following my tracks.
patches.replace: There was a warden there. He'd been following my tracks, and he'd lost the line as fast as I had. His hands were as white as mine.

open_errors.issue: In ch 16 Rohan says he told only Varun and the queen that he carries the seal ('No one else alive'). His ch 23 letter to Ila says 'I carry what you know the name of', which implies Ila knows about the seal.
open_errors.fix: Make the letter withhold the object rather than assume Ila knows it.

patches.find: I carry what you know the name of.
patches.replace: I carry a thing I will not name in a letter.

open_errors.issue: Meera loses her left ring and little fingers, leaving a thumb and two fingers. Ch 30 confirms 'three living fingers' on the left, counting the thumb. The made-to-measure glove in ch 31 is 'cut for a thumb and three fingers'. In ch 32 the same custom glove is said to have 'its empty stall'.
open_errors.fix: Cut the glove for a thumb and two fingers and drop the empty stall.

patches.find: a left glove of felted wool, lined with lambskin, cut for a thumb and three fingers.
patches.replace: a left glove of felted wool, lined with lambskin, cut for a thumb and two fingers.

patches.find: One young man looked at her left glove, with its empty stall, and then at the sky.
patches.replace: One young man looked at her left glove, with its two missing stalls, and then at the sky.

open_errors.issue: Meera wears Rohan's coat out of the lockhouse and on the salt road in ch 28 ('his borrowed coat'). The rope end, writ and tin are all in that coat. In ch 29 Rohan simply 'opened his coat' and finds the rope end, with no handback shown.
open_errors.fix: Note that Meera returned his coat at the halt.

patches.replace: Meera had handed his coat back at the halt. Rohan opened it.

open_errors.issue: Asha's crew is four people including Asha: Asha, Lalit and a second pair (ch 7 and ch 10). 'Asha and her four' makes five.

patches.find: He turned so that Asha and her four could see his face.
patches.replace: He turned so that Asha's four could see his face.

open_errors.issue: The Shilak Cairn is half a day's climb above Kothi Shilak (ch 1: 'at the cairn by noon'; ch 31 shows it apart from the village). In ch 32 Meera walks about fifteen spans from the cairn and reaches 'the goat pen gate', which reads as the salt-house pen in the village.
open_errors.fix: Make it a herders' fold near the cairn.

patches.find: She went on to the goat pen gate, and the creak of it told her she had gone far enough.
patches.replace: She went on to the herders' fold below the ring, and the creak of its gate told her she had gone far enough.
